critique.evidence: The screen advances the defense story by explicitly separating measured misses from evidence-quality caveats, reporting 69.6% recall, and attaching the residual gap to a concrete step-up/post-review control. However, it presents only one opaque gap (GPF-A21), provides no visible provenance or denominator for the recall figure, and does not connect the limitation to a specific intent-integrity attack, payment workflow, or Mastercard-relevant outcome. Successful API responses do not supply that missing relevance proof.
critique.fix: Turn GPF-A21 into an auditable Mastercard use-case entry: name the attack and affected payment/identity decision, show the evaluation source and miss numerator/denominator, distinguish observed misses from unmeasured evidence limitations, and quantify how the proposed step-up control reduces customer, fraud, or authorization risk.
